components.css: :root{--bg:#F2F4F6;--surface:#FFFFFF;--surface-2:#F6F8F9;--line:#D8DEE4;--line-soft:#E8ECF0;--line-strong:#AEB9C4;--text:#17212B;--text-2:#46535F;--text-3:#5F6D7A;--accent:#0F7662;--accent-mid:#8CC4B7;--red:#B42318;--red-soft:#FDECEA;--red-line:#F0B4AD;--amber-ink:#7A4A00;--amber-soft:#FFF4D6;--amber-line:#E5C36C;--track:#E1E6EB}.ds{font:400 16px/24px 'Source Sans 3',system-ui,sans-serif;color:var(--text)}.ds-tag{display:inline-flex;font:600 13px/18px inherit;font-family:inherit;padding:1px 8px;border-radius:4px;border:1px solid var(--line);background:var(--surface-2);color:var(--text-2)}.ds-tag.red{background:var(--red-soft);border-color:var(--red-line);color:var(--red)}.ds-tag.amber{background:var(--amber-soft);border-color:var(--amber-line);color:var(--amber-ink)}.ds-btn{font:600 15px/20px inherit;font-family:inherit;height:36px;padding:0 14px;border-radius:6px;border:1px solid transparent;display:inline-flex;align-items:center}.ds-btn.primary{background:var(--accent);color:#fff}.ds-btn.secondary{background:var(--surface);color:var(--text);border-color:var(--line-strong)}.ds-rec{display:inline-flex;flex-direction:column;gap:5px}.ds-track{display:block;width:148px;height:8px;border-radius:4px;background:var(--track);overflow:hidden}.ds-fill{display:block;height:100%;background:var(--accent);border-radius:4px}.ds-rec small{font-size:14px;line-height:20px;color:var(--text-2)}.ds-table{width:100%;border-collapse:collapse;background:var(--surface);border:1px solid var(--line)}.ds-table th,.ds-table td{text-align:left;padding:12px 20px;vertical-align:middle}.ds-table thead th{font:600 14px/20px inherit;font-family:inherit;color:var(--text-2);background:var(--surface-2);border-bottom:1px solid var(--line);padding-block:8px}.ds-table tbody th{font-size:17px;font-weight:700}

narrative.overview: The site looks and works like the patient-record software a physical therapist already uses. One thing per page: a table of patients, then one patient's chart in three tabs. Every action is a labelled button and nothing needs a legend. It replaced the Week Ring on Nov 16, 2026, which Matthew found confusing and AI-looking.
keyCharacteristics: White sheets on a light grey desk, separated by 1px hairlines. No dark surfaces.
Tables for anything that has rows.
One teal for primary buttons, the current tab and recovery progress.
Red and amber only on alerts and tags, always with the word.
One type family, Source Sans 3, tabular figures, no monospace.
The small recovery progress bar beside each patient is the one RECO touch.

rules.name: The One Teal Rule
rules.body: Teal means act here or recovery progress. It is never decoration, and no second accent is added.

rules.name: The Word Rule
rules.body: Red and amber never appear without the tier in words beside them.

rules.name: The Fixed Scale Rule
rules.body: Sizes are fixed pixels from the ramp. Nothing scales with the viewport except the page title on a phone.

rules.name: The One Thing Rule
rules.body: A page or a tab holds one subject. A second column of unrelated content becomes another tab.

rules.name: The One Shadow Rule
rules.body: Only the plan editor's publish bar is lifted, because it floats over the list.

dos: Give every action a labelled button; the page's main action is the only solid teal one.
Use a table when the content has rows and columns.
Pair every red or amber with the tier in words.
Keep one subject per page or tab.
Keep the recovery progress bar small and beside the patient.
donts: Don't bring back the Week Ring, a dark sidebar, diamonds or any chart that needs a legend.
Don't use monospace, or a font that draws zero with a slash.
Don't add a second accent colour, gradients or decorative shadows.
Don't show a percentage, a score or a risk level for a patient.
Don't count what a patient did or didn't do.
Don't use a coloured side stripe on a card or alert.
